subject: EdgeCare SSQ: access boundaries, PII classification, and cross-border evidence
messages:
From: Elena Smith <elena.smith@edgecare.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Cc: dpa@edgecare.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SSQ follow-up + required evidence for DPA annex

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our InfoSec team ran through Redwood's public materials and flagged a few items we need for our DPA annex and vendor review: a concise PII classification mapping for the product APIs, a dataflow diagram showing processing boundaries (we care about where KV cache/telemetry reside), and an inventory of subprocessors that touch tokenized inputs.

I've attached an initial spreadsheet with the specific questions (tab: "PII + Flow asks"). Can you confirm:
- Whether cached inference KV is ever written to persistent storage in hosted mode
- How we can evidence regional egress controls for EU customer data
- Which subprocessors handle telemetry vs. model hosting (we need names + purpose)

We are on a tight compliance timeline—our procurement lead needs these artifacts for the DPA annex by EOD Monday. If you need to loop legal/privacy from your side, please do.

Best,
Elena
Elena Smith
Head of Security Operations
EdgeCare Health

Attachment: EdgeCare_SSQ_initial_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet, 98KB)

From: ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
To: Elena Smith <elena.smith@edgecare.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSQ follow-up + required evidence for DPA annex

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Looping Marissa (Privacy & CS) and Rishi (Legal) to provide the artifacts and a short narrative for your procurement team. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Hosted mode KV cache: ephemeral in-memory caches are persisted to ephemeral local NVMe to serve active sessions but are never written to long-term object stores in our hosted offering; we can produce an architecture note and a short retention statement.
- Regional egress: we have region pinning and egress filters for EU customers; when a customer chooses an EU deployment, telemetry and model execution are confined to EU regions unless explicitly configured. We'll include a short export/evidence snippet showing the region routing policy.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach our current roster CSV and annotate which subprocessors handle telemetry, model hosting, monitoring, and logging.

Marissa/Rishi, can you prepare: (1) a one-page PII classification mapping for EdgeCare (PII categories -> API endpoints -> retention), (2) a redwood-dataflow-edgecare.svg highlighting KV/cache boundaries and egress controls, and (3) the subprocessor roster with purpose columns.

We should be able to get initial artifacts to you by Monday EOD PST. If procurement needs an interim confirmation earlier, tell me the required items and I can escalate.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0187

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Smith <elena.smith@edgecare.com>, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 03 Jul 2028 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft: PII mapping, dataflow diagram, and subprocessor roster (EdgeCare)

Elena / Ben — attached are the initial artifacts per Ben's note:
- PII mapping (sheet in attachment) outlines which endpoints may carry identifiers, classification labels, and retention policies.
- redwood-dataflow-edgecare.svg shows request ingress, model exec, KV cache boundary (ephemeral), telemetry pipeline, and egress control points.
- redwood-subprocessor-roster.csv lists subprocessors and the narrow purpose for each (model weights hosting, managed GPUs, telemetry ingestion, alerting).

Quick highlights and controlled language we recommend for the DPA annex:
- "Transient KV caches are stored on ephemeral instance storage and are not copied to durable object storage. Cache entries are evicted according to workload TTL policies and are scrubbed of user-provided PII after inference when configured by the customer."
- "For EU-region deployments, network egress is restricted to EU egress endpoints by default. Cross-border exports require customer opt-in and are logged in the audit trail."
- "Telemetry collected for performance (latency, error rates) is aggregated by default and does not contain user prompt text. If a customer enables full-text telemetry collection for debugging, that will be explicitly documented in the service configuration and covered by a separate processing agreement."

Notes / open items:
1) EdgeCare-specific retention window request: the spreadsheet asks for a 30-day prompt cache retention for session recovery — can you confirm if this is a hard requirement? If so, we will outline an architecture note for a dedicated EU-only cache (possible via Dedicated or Private deployments).
2) Subprocessor evidence: some partners require compliance attestations (SOC2) or region-specific contracts. If EdgeCare needs copies of SOC reports for particular subprocessors, tell us which ones and we'll coordinate with vendor relations to provide redacted attestations.

Attachment stubs: redwood-dataflow-edgecare.svg (diagram), redwood-subprocessor-roster.csv (6 rows), EdgeCare_SSQ_answers_v1.pdf (summary answers)

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Smith <elena.smith@edgecare.com>, marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft: PII mapping, dataflow diagram, and subprocessor roster (EdgeCare)

Elena — thanks for the quick review. Two legal confirmations to close the loop for procurement:

1) Data Transfers: Our Standard DPA includes a transfer annex that permits subprocessors in the US and EU as listed in the roster; for customers requiring SCCs or UK Addendum we have templates available. We will include the relevant export control language in the DPA annex draft.

2) Evidence: Redwood can provide (a) a redacted SOC 2 Type II report for primary cloud partners, (b) the subprocessor roster with purposes (attached), and (c) the network egress routing policy excerpt. We cannot share vendor contracts in full, but we can provide attestation letters where available.

Operationally, Marissa will own the technical artifacts; I will prepare the DPA annex language and a short cover note confirming that the ephemeral cache retention and EU egress controls meet EdgeCare's stated requirements (pending confirmation on the 30-day cache ask).

If EdgeCare confirms the 30-day requirement is negotiable (or can be met on Dedicated/Private), we'll flag that as a technical limitation for hosted customers and offer options.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
